methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: This bank did not merely deteriorate in FY2024 -- it failed. Percentage of Classified Investments exploded from 3.95% (FY2023) to 91.75% (FY2024, BDT 559,203.17mn of BDT 609,513.24mn total investment). Solo CRAR collapsed to 4.92% against a 12.50% requirement, with a Capital Surplus/(deficit) against Minimum Capital Requirement of BDT -29,228.15mn (i.e. the bank needed BDT 57,589.40mn of regulatory capital and had BDT 28,361.26mn). The auditor (Khan Wahab Shafique Rahman & Co.) issued a Qualified Opinion plus a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph, and separately calculated that if the full assessed provisioning shortfall were recognized, CRAR would fall to approximately (80.00)% to (80.39)%. Per Note 8.9, required provision against investments was BDT 494,979.21mn against BDT 16,361.94mn maintained (deficit BDT 478,617.27mn = 47,861.73 crore) -- Bangladesh Bank explicitly permitted the bank to publish these audited financial statements without booking this deficit (letter DOS(CAMS)1157/41(Dividend)/2025-3100 dated 21/05/2025). FY2024 profit after tax was BDT -3,993.40mn (EPS -3.31) vs +3,240.09mn (EPS 2.82) in FY2023. Subsequent events (outside the FY2024 report but confirmed via DSE disclosures and independent web research): Bangladesh Bank declared the bank 'non-viable' and suspended trading effective 5 November 2025 under the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025; on 9 November 2025 Bangladesh Bank issued a Letter of Intent merging this bank with Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank (also in this dataset) into a new state-owned entity, 'Sammilito Islami Bank'; a Capital Reduction Order dated 21 December 2025 wrote the bank's entire paid-up capital (BDT 1,208.14 crore) down to ZERO and cancelled all shares, effective 5 November 2025; the bank was placed in DSE 'Z' category on 4 January 2026 for failing to hold its FY2024 AGM. No FY2025 annual report exists or is expected to -- see data_gaps. This is the most severe single-year/single-bank deterioration found anywhere in this 36-bank dataset to date, exceeding even NBL's FY2024 balance-sheet insolvency (equity -24,003mn, CAR -5.48%) and ISLAMIBANK's FY2024 under-provisioning (884,350mn unprovided = 12.7x equity) in that FIRSTSBANK's institutional existence itself did not survive past FY2024.

The FY2024 Auditors' Report's 'Other Matters' section documents, in the auditor's own words: (1) 'irregular investment disbursements... involving the use of borrower identities that may not have reflected actual customers' with 'a portion of the disbursed funds may have been misappropriated', Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) legal proceedings and asset freezes against bank officials, and a Bangladesh Bank forensic audit with a special task force and international auditors engaged to trace fund movements; (2) investment proceeds used to settle liabilities of 'other entities under common control' with 'patterns of inter-borrower fund transfers' disguised as unrelated transactions; (3) inadequately disclosed contingent liabilities tied to the classified-investment portfolio; (4) overvaluation of collateral (particularly land) 'exceeding actual purchase or mouza values'; (5) investment disbursements exceeding sanctioned limits via unauthorized internal 'Commitment IDs' issued by Head Office without formal amendments; and (6) undocumented placement agreements with Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC, Rupali Bank PLC, and Janata Bank PLC. Separately, the Emphasis of Matter section describes IT-control failures: 'The Bank's CIPPS was manipulated to enhance investment limits without proper approval.' This is direct auditor-sourced evidence (not third-party allegation) of the S. Alam Group-era related-party lending abuse flagged as a governance risk in this bank's FY2019 report (see the related_party_governance_signal below), now realized.

The FY2024 audited financial statements contain unreconciled internal inconsistencies, recorded here verbatim rather than reconciled, per project convention. (a) Note 8.9 and the Auditors' Report's 'Basis for Qualified Opinion' both cite the SAME Bangladesh Bank letter (DBI-06/51(2)/2025-373 dated 27/04/2025) but state different required-provision figures: BDT 49,497.92 crore (Note 8.9) vs BDT 50,994.06 crore (Auditors' Report), a BDT 1,496.34 crore difference. (b) Three different classified-investment figures coexist in the same document: 91.75% / BDT 559,203.17mn (Annexure-B, 'Amount of Classified Investments'); 83.24% / BDT 507,341.46mn (Note 8.9's CL-classification base: Sub-standard + Doubtful + Bad&Loss); and ~81% / ~BDT 494,390mn (the Auditors' Report's going-concern paragraph). None of the three is flagged in the source document as superseding another.

Investment-Deposit ratio jumped from 103.13% (FY2022) to 118.45% (FY2023) as total deposits fell (BDT 473,046mn -> BDT 455,195mn) while investments kept growing — a level well above the typical <100% norm seen in FY2011-2019 (peak 93.15% in FY2018) and a liquidity-strain signal. This continued into FY2024: IDR reached 122.25% even as total deposits fell further to BDT 431,431.01mn, and the Auditors' Report separately disclosed a Liquidity Coverage Ratio of just 22.75% (required >=100%) and a Net Stable Funding Ratio of 71.80% (required >100%) at FY2024 year-end.

Percentage of Classified Investments (this bank's NPL-equivalent) rose from 4.39% (FY2020) to a peak of 4.73% (FY2021), then improved to 3.95% (FY2023) — a milder and more contained pattern than the sharp FY2024 spikes seen at conventional banks in this dataset at the time. This proved to be the calm before the collapse: see regulatory_resolution_and_failure_fy2024_fy2025 above for the FY2024 explosion to 91.75%.

Newly-added Q1-Q3 un-audited interim filings (added 2026-08-27) show the FY2024 collapse was NOT a single hidden event -- it was a real, accelerating, quantifiable deterioration visible in the bank's own quarterly disclosures from Q2 2024 onward, culminating in a sudden catastrophic recognition specifically in Q4. Discrete-quarter Net Profit After Tax (Solo): Q1 2024 +BDT 361.03mn, Q2 2024 +BDT 528.20mn (still growing), Q3 2024 -BDT 274.93mn (the first quarterly LOSS, filed/signed 2024-10-31, versus +BDT 363.98mn in the same quarter of 2023) -- Total Operating Income (discrete) nearly halved year-over-year in Q3 alone (BDT 2,380.54mn vs BDT 3,628.80mn). Cumulative 9-month (Jan-Sep 2024) profit was still positive at +BDT 614.30mn. Subtracting this from the already-stored FY2024 full-year loss (BDT -3,993.40mn, from 2024_Q4.json) implies a Q4-2024-alone (Oct-Dec) loss of approximately BDT -4,607.70mn -- 115% of the entire reported annual loss, meaning the full-year loss is smaller in magnitude than the implied Q4 loss alone because Q1-Q3 was net profitable. A leading indicator was visible even earlier and accelerating fast: cumulative 'Specific Provision for Classified Investment' (the only asset-quality-adjacent figure disclosed at interim frequency by this bank) went BDT +144.53mn (Q1) -> +593.78mn (H1, i.e. +449.25mn in Q2 alone, 3.1x Q1's charge) -> +1,800.39mn (9m, i.e. +1,206.61mn in Q3 alone, 2.7x Q2's charge) -- roughly tripling quarter-on-quarter, a full 7-8 months before the FY2024 audited financial statements (finalized ~2025-05-29) revealed Classified Investments had reached 91.75% and Solo CRAR had collapsed to 4.92%. CRITICALLY, no Classified-Investment percentage or CRAR figure is disclosed in ANY of this bank's un-audited interim (Q1/H1/Q3) filings at any point in 2024 or any other year -- these headline crisis metrics only ever surfaced in the year-end audited statements, meaning a market participant reading only the interim filings would have seen mounting stress (accelerating provisions, a swing to a quarterly loss) but had no way to see the true 91.75%/4.92% scale until the audit. The crisis did not stop at FY2024 year-end: subsequently-filed un-audited Q1 2025 (signed 2025-05-29, the same day the audited FY2024 statements were adopted) and Q2 2025 (signed 2025-07-30) filings show losses of BDT -5,755.73mn and BDT -11,170.09mn respectively -- each individually larger than the entire FY2024 annual loss -- driven in Q1 2025 by Net Investment Income itself turning negative (Profit Paid on Deposits of BDT 10,424.43mn EXCEEDING Investments Income of BDT 6,852.81mn), eroding Solo Total Shareholders' Equity from BDT 20,069.13mn (31-Dec-2024) to just BDT 3,143.31mn (30-Jun-2025) -- i.e. down to roughly 26% of paid-up capital alone -- months before Bangladesh Bank's Capital Reduction Order (effective 5-Nov-2025) formally wrote capital to zero.

Several directors profiled in the FY2019 annual report hold concurrent director/shareholder positions across numerous S. Alam Group-affiliated companies (S. Alam Cement, S. Alam Steels, S. Alam Vegetable Oil, S. Alam Power Plant, S. Alam Properties, and others). This is the same conglomerate whose related-party lending exposure is documented to have caused a severe FY2024 asset-quality and capital-adequacy shock at EXIM Bank (also in this dataset) following Bangladesh's 2024 political transition. This forecast is now confirmed and realized: see regulatory_resolution_and_failure_fy2024_fy2025 and auditor_fraud_findings_fy2024 above -- this bank was placed under Bangladesh Bank resolution in November 2025 and merged into a new state-owned bank alongside EXIM Bank and three other S. Alam-linked Islamic banks.

historical_context: First Security Islami Bank ran a conventional, moderately-growing Islamic banking franchise from FY2011-2023 (assets BDT 91,013mn to BDT 659,114mn, classified investments consistently under 5%), with an emerging FY2023 liquidity-strain signal (deposits falling while investments grew) set against a governance backdrop of heavy S. Alam Group director overlap. FY2024 is where the S. Alam Group-linked related-party lending abuse, already documented as a severe FY2024 shock at EXIM Bank elsewhere in this dataset, hit this bank directly and catastrophically: classified investments exploded to 91.75% of the portfolio, Solo CRAR collapsed to 4.92% (vs 12.5% required, and as low as -80% on a fully-provisioned basis per the auditor), and the FY2024 Auditors' Report documents auditor-identified fraud patterns (fictitious borrower identities, inter-related-party fund transfers, ACC criminal proceedings, a Bangladesh Bank forensic audit). Unlike every other bank in this dataset, FIRSTSBANK's story does not continue into FY2025 as the same entity: Bangladesh Bank declared it non-viable in November 2025 and merged it, with zero residual share value, into a new state-owned bank ('Sammilito Islami Bank') together with Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank. This makes FIRSTSBANK's FY2024 figures a rare directly-observed 'end state' of the exact mechanism (S. Alam Group related-party lending) that this dataset's insights for EXIM Bank and other banks could previously only infer was in progress.
data_gaps: UPDATED 2026-08-27: Q1/Q2(Half-Yearly)/Q3 un-audited interim data has now been researched and added for FY2018-2025 (FY2011-2017 attempted separately via Wayback -- see sources.json for exact year-by-year outcome), sourced from the bank's own fsibplc.com quarterly/half-yearly filings (2021-2025, live) and the Wayback Machine for the pre-2021 fsiblbd.com domain (2018-2020). One quarter (2018 Q3) could not be recovered -- all five independent Wayback captures of that specific document share an identical, genuinely-corrupted content digest (not a crawl-truncation artifact). No Classified-Investment percentage or CRAR/CRAR-equivalent ratio is disclosed in ANY un-audited interim filing this bank has published, in any year -- only in year-end audited statements; the closest available interim asset-quality proxy is 'Specific Provision for Classified Investment', a cumulative P&L note sub-line, present from FY2019 onward but not broken out separately in FY2018 or earlier interim filings. DSE disclosures separately show a revised, unaudited Q3 2025 (Jan-Sep 2025) Consolidated NAV per share of Tk (460.18) -- this specific data point was NOT re-verified or turned into a 2025_Q3.json in this pass (time-boxed; the underlying primary PDF was not located on fsibplc.com, which stopped publishing new Q3 filings after the bank's November 2025 resolution). FY2025 has no annual report and, per independent confirmation via the EXIMBANK agent working this same dataset plus this agent's own web research, is very unlikely to ever get one under the 'FIRSTSBANK' entity: the bank was merged into the new state-owned 'Sammilito Islami Bank' in November 2025 before FY2025 even closed. This is recorded in sources.json as 'researched_confirmed_unavailable', not 'not_started' -- it is a probable permanent series-end, not a routine lag, and future sessions should not keep re-searching for it without new information (e.g. a Sammilito Islami Bank filing that separately discloses FIRSTSBANK's standalone FY2025 position). Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) is still not available for FY2020-2023 (the source tables for those years report Total Capital Fund in absolute terms but not the ratio, and Risk Weighted Assets was not extracted for those years) -- but IS now available for FY2024 (4.92%, Solo), the first year this dataset has it for this bank; note that this FY2024 report's own comparative column additionally shows FY2023 Solo CRAR was 11.91%, which is not written back into the existing 2023_Q4.json per this project's rule against editing already-stored years, but is recorded here for a future session that may want to backfill it. ROE is calculated throughout (not reported by the bank in its own summary tables).
